earlier_scan.source_named: Bouny, P. 1977. Inventaire phonetique d'un parler Kotoko: le Mandague de Mara. In Caprile (ed.), Etudes Phonologiques Tchadiennes, 59-77. Paris: SELAF.

sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: 13A Tone = 'Simple tone system' (source Bouny 1977); no stress features (14A-17A) coded for this language.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Afade stress; §8.4.2 (p. 216): 'There is no published work on Afade, except for the comparative studies by Tourneux (2001; 2003), though there are wordlists collected by Lebeuf (1942), and Allison (n.d.)'; gives Afade surface vowels and ejectives only; the reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress.

sources.citation: Allison, Sean David. 2012. Aspects of a Grammar of Makary Kotoko (Chadic, Cameroon). PhD dissertation, University of Colorado at Boulder.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Describes Mpade (Makary Kotoko), not Afade; Afade appears only in the Kotoko classification table (§1.1) and in examples as a place name; no statement about Afade prosody.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2005 [2004]. Les marques personnelles en kotoko et en mafa/wandala (langues tchadiques de la branche centrale). In Ibriszimow & Segerer (eds), Systèmes de marques personnelles en Afrique (HAL halshs-00349287).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes 'inversion du schème tonal entre Afa / Gou et l'ensemble du groupe central' and that accusative vs dative object pronouns differ only in tone.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2005. « L'Enfant Terrible d'Afadé (Cameroun) : version masculine / version féminine ». In Baumgardt & Derive (eds), Paroles nomades : Écrits d'ethnolinguistique africaine (HAL halshs-00349286).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; ethnolinguistic study of two Afade tales (French translation in this deposit); fn.1 says the Afade data were collected in Cameroon 1990-1993 (ORSTOM/IRD).

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2003 [publ. 2006]. Origine des consonnes doubles et de la nasale syllabique à l'initiale dans les parlers « kotoko » du Cameroun. Topics in Chadic Linguistics II (HAL halshs-00349264).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; refers to 'ton haut'/'ton bas' features of syllables; tone-marked Kotoko data.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2003. La numération dans les parlers « kotoko » du Cameroun (halshs-00349283); 2003. L'encodage de la localisation.. (halshs-00349311); 2003. Pluralité nominale, pluralité verbale et marques aspectuelles en « kotoko » [Zina data] (halshs-00349305); Tourneux & Mahamat 2007 [2009]. Les marqueurs relatifs.. (halshs-00458668); Tourneux 2021. Le nom du souverain dans les parlers « kotoko » du Cameroun (halshs-03473327).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress in any of them; Afade (Afa) forms cited with lexical/grammatical tone marks; tonal schemes discussed for plural and imperfective marking (Zina).

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2001 [publ. 2003]. Le système consonantique des langues dites « kotoko ». 1st Biennial International Colloquium on the Chadic Language Family, Leipzig 2001, pp. 115-135 (HAL halshs-00349309).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Afade (afadé /'afa/) phoneme chart and all Afade forms are given with H/L tone marks; §5 Remarques: the initial nasal in NC- is syllabic 'quand le ton qu'elle porte est différent de celui de la syllabe qui suit' (rem. 3) and 'Il y a une fréquente inversion du schème tonal entre afadé et maltam' (rem. 12) -- i.e. Afade is treated as a tone language.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2000 [publ. 2003]. Le système vocalique dans le groupe « kotoko ». Actes du 3e Congrès mondial de linguistique africaine, Lomé 2000 (HAL halshs-00349308).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; vowel qualities derived from /a, ə/ plus word-level palatalisation/labialisation 'prosodies'; data tone-marked.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, Afade (afad1236): inventory 'KOTOKO' (UPSID 198) from Bouny 1977; Wikipedia (en) 'Afade language' phonology section from Bouny 1977.
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept

sources.note: Historical ethnographic report; says only that the Affadéh language 'hat einige Laute, welche für mich völlig unaussprechlich waren'; no accent statement located in the scanned (the vocabulary itself appeared in Vater 1816).
